messages.subject: sparseQuant analysis error
parts:
Hi Olga, Meena and Veavi,
sorry about posting this issue here in the MSstats discussion group, but I believe that sparseQuant does not have its own group yet and here is my best bet for getting help. Basically, I'm trying to run sparseQuant (version 1.1) with rStudio (0.98.977) using a mac OSX 10.9, on a SILAC-spiked SRM data and I can't make the 'analysis' function to work. I first tried some of the examples datasets and the MouseLiver and Spike-in worked like a charm (plots and Rdata output). However, with the Eico dataset, only the plots and the ImputeData Rdata are generated (no TestResult and FittedData). Using my own dataset, things got worst ... only the QC profile plots were generated, while the Boxplot pdf was corrupted. And all the Rdata were not generated as well. The data is a little complex and I could send it offline. There are 6 different Conditions and I am making only 3 comparisons (no overlap for now).  
I also tried to run the source code stepwise, and noticed that the ".imputeAnalyze" function (sparseQuant_mainFunction.R, line 164) does not generate any object. The function runs for a few seconds, and ends without any on-screen error. Because my rStudio seemed a little buggy, I also tried my R Console (R version 3.0.2). Here, the 'analysis' function generates an error (below). 

I would greatly appreciate your help. 
Thank you very much
Alex


When I run the function with the plot options, I got the following error:

> analysis(sparseData1, refPep, comparison, qualityControlPlot=TRUE,evaluationPlot=TRUE, address="Output/analysis1_")
Error in rep(j, temp1[j]) : invalid 'times' argument

I then run the function without plots and got the following error:
> analysis(sparseData1, refPep, comparison, qualityControlPlot=FALSE,evaluationPlot=FALSE, address="Output/analysis1_")
Error in data.frame(impute.h, impute.y = NA, impute.index = TRUE) : 
  arguments imply differing number of rows: 0, 1

Finally, I run the debug() function and got this:

            "postVar", "sampleVar", "weight")]

            sep = ""))

        ImputeData$sampleVar <- 1

        }

            "L"]

        ImputeData[ImputeData$Label == "L", "Subject"] <- ImputeData$Subject_Original[ImputeData$Label == 
            "L"]
        ImputeData$Subject <- factor(ImputeData$Subject)
        ImputeData$Run <- factor(ImputeData$Run)
        ImputeData <- data.frame(ImputeData, Subject_Nested = paste(ImputeData[, 
            "Group"], ImputeData[, "Subject"], sep = "."))
        temp <- unique(ImputeData[, c("Group", "Subject")])
        temp <- temp[with(temp, order(Group, Subject)), ]
        temp <- data.frame(temp, Subject_Nested = paste(temp[, 
            "Group"], temp[, "Subject"], sep = "."))
        ImputeData$Subject_Nested <- factor(ImputeData$Subject_Nested, 
            levels = temp$Subject_Nested)
        ImputeData <- ImputeData[, c("Protein", "Peptide", "Transition", 
            "Feature", "Label", "Group_Original", "Subject_Original", 
            "Run", "Intensity100", "Intensity", "impute_Intensity", 
            "index_Intensity", "Group", "Subject", "Subject_Nested", 
            "postVar", "sampleVar", "weight")]
        save(ImputeData, file = paste(address, "ImputeData.RData", 
            sep = ""))
    }
    temp <- .groupComparisonAnalyze(ImputeData, comparison, scope)
    TestResult <- temp$result
    FittedData <- temp$data
    save(FittedData, file = paste(address, "FittedData.RData", 
        sep = ""))
    save(TestResult, file = paste(address, "TestResult.RData", 
        sep = ""))
    if (evaluationPlot == TRUE) {
        .Evaluation_ResidualPlots(FittedData, address)
        .Evaluation_PredictionPlots(ImputeData, sparseRefPep, 
            address)
    }
}
